title: Objects and their syntactic types
source_location: ISO printed pp.114–115, §7.9.1 (PDF physical pp.129–130); 7.9.2.1 printed p.115
errata: No direct §7.9.1 erratum located. EC3 #322 updates Table 35 terminology but does not remove §7.9.2.1's sentence that the single PDF string is further qualified by context.
code: crates/pdf-syntax/src/object.rs Object::String (byte storage); crates/pdf-syntax/src/text_string.rs typed decoding helpers; consumers decide decoding based on property context
tests: crates/pdf-model/tests/text_strings_spec_audit.rs covers text-string fields and text-stream decoding; tree key tests assert bytes. Content-string operands have separate font character-code path and are not PDF text strings by default.
assertions: Existing text audit asserts decoded rendered output for field values; `trees_rectangles_audit.rs::name_tree_lookup_uses_exact_bytes_and_distinguishes_prefixes` checks raw name-tree bytes but its Names array is correctly byte-sorted A, a, a-NUL, decomposed e-acute, composed é. The separate query loop is not the stored ordering.
residuals: No single type-level runtime validator can determine intended string qualification; correct context dispatch must be audited at each property consumer. This shard excludes language-escape syntax and dates. Existing PDFDocEncoded /Status bug was fixed by b901326c (`FormsData::read` now uses `pdf_doc_encoded_string`); do not repeat that stale finding.

title: Text, ASCII and byte strings are context-specific qualifications of one string object
source_location: ISO printed pp.115–117, §§7.9.2.1–7.9.2.4 (PDF physical pp.130–132); verify printed footer for exact subheading locator before later citation
errata: EC3 #322 changes Table 35 text but leaves §7.9.2.1 body sentence intact. Language escape rules are outside this assignment.
code: crates/pdf-syntax/src/text_string.rs; consumers in page_label.rs, forms_data.rs and destination.rs use context-specific entry points; name tree uses bytes unchanged
tests: crates/pdf-model/tests/text_strings_spec_audit.rs; crates/pdf-syntax/tests/trees_rectangles_audit.rs exact byte lookup test; current language tests are parent-added, not evidence of prior/baseline coverage.
assertions: String property tests compare resulting Unicode or rendered value; tree query compares raw bytes. No audit-level assertion should assume every Object::String is UTF-8 or is text.
verdict: ledger claims generally backed by context-specific code and targeted assertions; no defect found in sampled scope
residuals: Full matrix of consumers and every field's qualification not certified. Excluded language escapes, dates, and property-specific clauses; no blanket §7.9.2 certification.

title: String keys differ from dictionary Name keys; arbitrary values
source_location: ISO §7.9.6 opening bullets, printed p.119 (physical p.134), lines 3516–3521 in processed markdown
errata: EC3 #214 strikes lexical wording but retains explicit byte-prefix/equality rules; #307 adds producer prohibition on null keys. Null-key prohibition does not require a reader to reject a malformed tree.
code: crates/pdf-syntax/src/tree.rs TreeKey::Name compares Object::String byte slices; name_pairs retains keys as Vec<u8>; value objects are passed through/resolved according to consumer
assertions: Byte equality and prefix cases are useful, but synthetic Names sequence is byte-sorted; it tests exact byte keys in a valid flat tree, but does not exercise Kids/Limits through a PDF public consumer. Null-key test evaluates tolerant pair preservation for producer-invalid data only.
verdict: implementation evidence supports representation and equality; valid public path lacks byte-sorted multi-level fixture
residuals: No reader-side rejection or diagnostics for null keys is required by the producer-directed erratum. Key-display decoding is a consumer question, not tree comparison.

title: Root, intermediate, and leaf node forms; Kids children are indirect references
source_location: ISO §7.9.6 paragraph and Table 36, printed pp.119–120 (physical pp.134–135), processed lines 3523–3531
errata: EC3 #307 null key applies at leaf key level; no change to Kids shape identified.
code: crates/pdf-syntax/src/tree.rs::descend accepts Kids and recursively visits resolved child dictionaries; attachment tree writer emits canonical single root leaf; transform writer paths preserve/write trees
tests: tree.rs::a_key_is_found_through_intermediate_nodes tests nested search but constructs Kids with direct dictionaries, contrary to the Table 36 producer form. `trees_rectangles_audit.rs` covers byte lookup only. Writer tests cover flat one-node trees.
assertions: Existing deep traversal demonstrates recursive mechanics but is not a valid-conformance fixture. Reader tolerance for direct Kids is not a defect. No valid exact-xref public consumer test was found for deep indirect name-tree nodes.
verdict: implementation is present; assertion gap for valid multi-level indirect tree through a public consumer
residuals: Node producer constraints do not imply that malformed input must be rejected. Need valid deep public test; drafted Destination name-tree test.

title: Bytewise key identity/order, contiguous leaves, exact extrema and traversal
source_location: ISO §7.9.6 ordering paragraphs and Table 36, printed pp.120–121 (physical pp.135–136), processed lines 3530–3535
errata: EC3 #214 withdraws the word lexical from ordering cells/text. Remaining text explicitly requires shorter common-prefix keys first, consistent encoding, byte-by-byte equality; operational ordering is byte lexicographic. #307 adds null-key writer constraint.
code: TreeKey::Name uses slice Ord; `admits` consults low/high Limits to skip excluded children; `collect` enumerates leaf pairs; `lookup` descends rather than flattening
tests: `name_tree_lookup_uses_exact_bytes_and_distinguishes_prefixes` tests raw prefix/case/composed byte differences in a correctly sorted Names array; tree.rs `a_key_is_found_through_intermediate_nodes` uses an invalid direct child structure. No assertion found that combines sorted exact byte keys, valid exact Limits, indirect Kids, and public lookup.
assertions: Malformed Limits tests document tolerant behavior: missing hint widens lookup and an excluding false hint may lose the key. They do not test valid producers or require validation. Writer sort test checks byte prefix order.
verdict: comparison and search are code-supported; valid deep public assertion gap
residuals: Limits are treated as a search gate when present and contradictory; reader does not validate exact extrema. The standard places those requirements on producers, so absent validation is not automatically a reader failure. Consider whether malformed false Limits should be recovered, but separate local policy from ISO conformance.

title: Values may be any object; stream values shall be indirect, selected complex values should be indirect
source_location: ISO §7.9.6 opening bullets, printed p.119 (physical p.134), processed lines 3518–3521
code: generic tree reader preserves values; output attachment writer uses the canonical tree_root helper and existing file-spec references
tests: writer and attachment tests verify paired values/file references; they do not enumerate every possible object category
assertions: The clause says streams shall be indirect but says dictionary/array/string should be indirect; other simple values should be direct. Those latter SHOULD producer conventions do not imply reader rejection. No standalone stream-value tree fixture found in this shard.
verdict: generic representation supported; no reader defect established
residuals: Writer reachability for each values category was not exhaustively inventoried. Stream indirectness is mandatory for producers; reader rejection/reporting not specified here.

title: Integer keys, Nums naming and ascending numerical order
source_location: ISO §7.9.7 opening paragraph and Table 37, printed pp.122–123 (physical pp.137–138), processed lines 3563–3570
errata: EC3 #307 adds `Keys shall not be the null object` to Table 37 /Nums. #214 concerns name-tree wording only; number keys remain ascending numeric.
ledger: number-tree-difference, number-tree-shape, number-tree-kids, number-tree-pairs, number-tree-order, number-tree-limits, number-tree-name-alias
code: TreeKey::Number compares i64; `number_pairs` collects Nums and retains traversal order; archive NumberTree extension validates ordering and emits Nums
tests: tree.rs::a_number_trees_pairs_come_back_in_order checks paired numeric values but Kids are direct dictionaries; page-label tests cover flat /Nums root; archive writer tests cover indirect leaves and ordering.
assertions: Current public consumer coverage tests only flat number trees. `number_pairs` not sorting input is consistent with required producer order; PageLabels later sorting is tolerance and not reader-error policy.
verdict: implementation supported; valid deep public number-tree consumer assertion gap
residuals: Draft page-label public test exercises valid indirect nodes and numeric order. No demand for rejecting unsorted/null keys based solely on producer constraints.

title: Lookup traverses selected branches; listing consumers enumerate pairs
source_location: ISO §7.9.6 opening bullet, printed p.119 / physical p.134; processed lines 3520–3521
errata: No direct erratum changes the efficiency requirement.
code: tree.rs::lookup descends Kids using Limits; name_pairs/number_pairs enumerate. Destination::named is lookup; attachment and PageLabels consumers enumerate.
tests: Existing deep tree test uses direct Kids dictionaries; page-label/destination consumer cases are flat. New drafts provide valid indirect deep trees.
assertions: Destination draft checks both branches; PageLabels draft verifies enumerated ranges. Drafts are not execution evidence.
verdict: code paths present; valid deep public-consumer assertion gap addressed by drafts
residuals: No fanout complexity benchmark. ISO does not prescribe binary search or a complexity bound; no demonstrated conformance defect.

feature: 7.9.6 Names pair arrays and root/leaf selection
title: Names is alternating string-key/value pairs; root uses either Names or Kids
source_location: ISO §7.9.6 paragraph and Table 36, printed pp.119–120 / physical pp.134–135; processed lines 3523–3531
errata: EC3 #307 adds no-null-key writer constraint; #214 changes order wording, not pair structure.
code: tree.rs::collect pairs by chunks_exact(2), TreeKey::entries selects Names; attachment tree_root writes a one-node Names root.
tests: Null-key unit checks pair preservation on malformed input; writer test covers flat sorted output. Neither is a valid deep producer fixture.
assertions: Destination draft has a root Kids node and indirect Leaves with string keys and indirect destination values.
verdict: reader pairing and flat canonical writer supported; no reader rejection is implied for invalid source
residuals: No full producer-shape validator; transform/archive writer paths not exhaustively enumerated.

title: Limits give exact extrema and tree leaves cover non-overlapping contiguous ranges
source_location: ISO §7.9.6 paragraph after Table 36, printed p.120 / physical p.135; processed lines 3533–3535
code: tree.rs::admits compares low/high keys and skips excluded subtrees; flat writer has no child ranges.
tests: Existing Limits unit includes missing and deliberately false Limits, both malformed-policy cases. Draft name tree includes exact [(A),(a)] and [(b),(z)] ranges matching sorted keys.
assertions: New destination test would assert keys in both legal branches. Page-label draft uses exact [0,2] and [10,10] numeric ranges.
verdict: valid ranges represented in candidate drafts; reader does not validate extrema/partition
residuals: False Limits currently hide keys. Whether to recover is reader policy; producer constraints alone do not mandate reader rejection or recovery.

title: Number-tree root/leaf/intermediate shape and indirect Kids
source_location: ISO Table 37, printed pp.122–123 / physical pp.137–138; processed lines 3563–3574
errata: EC3 #307 adds no-null-key producer rule to Nums.
code: shared tree.rs traversal; archive NumberTree::extended writes indirect appended leaves and Limits; flat number-tree writer may use root Nums.
tests: Existing number tree traversal unit uses direct child dictionaries and does not model valid Kids. Archive writer tests inspect indirect output leaves.
assertions: PageLabels draft uses indirect root Kids [15 0 R 19 0 R], exact leaf limits, Nums arrays, indirect value dictionaries, and independent page-label outputs.
verdict: implementation supported; valid deep public input assertion drafted
residuals: No reader validator/rejection obligation for producer-form violations inferred.
